 JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84908815/
1 payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
On 30.07.2024 at about 5.50 a.m., the petitioner along with her relative were p r o c e e d i n g i n h i s H e r o H o n d a P a s s i o n P r o m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-17-EW-2716 near Aiyyappa Temple Corner, HMT Main Road,
Yeshwanthapura.
At that time one Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3589 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle from behind.
Due to impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted KC General Hospital, Malleshwaram Bengaluru and then shifted to ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he was discharged with an advice for continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.
4. The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 38 years as on the date of accident.
He was working as IISC 'C' Yashwanthpura, Bengaluru through Shakti Kitchen Pvt Ltd., as a Contract Employee and was earning Rs.21,000/- per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driver of the respondent, who drive his vehicle Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3589.
The respondent is the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and accident has taken place due to the negligent drive of the offender bus driver.
Hence the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till the realization.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
7. After registration of the petition, notice was issued against respondent.
In pursuance of service of notice the respondent has appeared through its counsel and has filed its written statement on behalf of respondent by denying the entire petition averments.

Further denied the age of the petitioner,
avocation and income of the said petitioner.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
8. In order to substantiate his claim, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 28 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.28.

The petitioner submitted that there was no further petitioner Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84908815/
2 evidence, the further petitioner evidence was taken as closed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent has examined it driver as RW.1 and has not got marked any documents on his behalf and the case was posted for arguments.

9. Heard the arguments on both side and perused the materials on record.
10.
Based on the above said pleading, this tribunal has framed the following issues:

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57-F-3589 by its driver, in RTA took place on 30.07.2024 at about 5.50 a.m., on Chikkagondanahalli Gate, Hassan-Bengaluru on HMT Main Road, near Ayyappa Temple Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount and from whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
11. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;

Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per the final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
12. The petitioner has made stand towards fact and factum of the accident that on 30.07.2024 at about 5.50 a.m., the petitioner along with her relative were proceeding in his Hero Honda Passion Pro motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-EW-2716 near Aiyyappa Temple Corner, HMT Main Road,
Yeshwanthapura.
At that time one Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3589 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle from behind.
Due to impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. The petitioner has claimed compensation against the respondents urging that the alleged accident took place on the alleged date, time, place and thereby the petitioner was called upon to substantiate the said stand.
14. By responding to the one way burden the petitioner has come up with oral and documentary evidence.
The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 28 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.28.

In her chief-examination, PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments and has specifically Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84908815/
3 stated that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offender vehicle.

entities.text: Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondent.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
16. The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint,
Ex.P.11 is the rough sketch, Ex.P.12 is the Spot mahazar, Ex.P23 is the IMV report and Ex.P8 is the Charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
17. The above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-3589.
It is clear from the records that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and extended with treatment.
There is no any adverse material available to disbelieve the stand taken by the petitioner to the extent of the factum of accident as introduced by him.
Thus, this tribunal has answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.
In support of the case petitioner has come up with various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.

1. Pecuniary loss:- This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.

(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-
In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate which is marked as per Ex.P.3.
As per the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
The Ex.P.4 is the discharge summary which shows that the petitioner was admitted to hospital from 30.07.2024 to 10.08.2024 for a period of 11 days.

These documents shows that petitioners have taken treatment in ESIC Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84908815/
4 Hospital, Rajajinagar, Bengaluru, but the doctor is not examined by petitioner.
Without the examination of the doctor it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any injuries.

entities.text: ESIC Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that though non examination of the doctor by the petitioner is not fatal to the case but without the assessment of the disability by the doctor it is impossible to believe that the petitioner has sustained the injuries narrated in the petition.
Thereby the petitioner is not entitled to compensation towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner was self employed and used to earn Rs.21,000/- per month.
As the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove the income.
In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and operated for the year-2024.
Under the circumstances, the per day income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.550/-.
As per the discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to hospital as an inpatient for 11 days and after discharge from the hospital there must be necessary to take bed rest for at least 49 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate which comes to Rs.66,000/- (60 days X 550 = Rs.33,000 + 33,000).
(B) Medical expenditure:-

The petitioner has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance,
medical treatment, attendant and other expenses.
The petitioner has not produced the medical bills.
Hence, he is not entitled for the same.
(D) Conveyance allowances, food, nourishment and special diet:-
As per the available material it is clear that the petitioner was under treatment for a period of 11 days.
This shows that petitioner has incurred expenditure towards conveyance, food, nourishment and special diet to meet the treatment.

Under the circumstances if the conveyance charges fixed at Rs.1,000/- per day then it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.11,000/- (Rs.1,000/- X 11 days) towards conveyance allowance, food, nourishment and special diet.

(e) Pain and sufferings and mental agony:-
According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained injuries as on the date of accident.
The said accidental injuries have caused lot of pain to suffer in the future life span.
Pain and suffering would be categorized as a non-pecuniary loss as it is incapable of being arithmetically calculated.

Therefore, when compensation is to be awarded for pain and suffering, special circumstances of the claimant have to be Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84908815/
5 taken into account including the victim's age, the unusual deprivation the victim has suffered, the effect thereof on his or her future life.

entities.text: Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the nature of the injuries caused to the petitioner.
Hence the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

(f) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
This includes a variety of matters such as the inability to walk, run or sit, etc.
This shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of the personal life and amenities of life.
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- under this head.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.1,22,000/- which is just and proper.
19. Admittedly, the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, respondent is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
Prahlad vs B.M.T.C on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84908815/
6 ORDER

sentences.text: The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,22,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in her favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
